about: The expert council, item 4 (queue expert-council): family PACE plans. Soldiers and diplomats never rely on one way of doing a vital thing: they name a Primary, an Alternate, a Contingency and an Emergency way, in advance, and rehearse the switch. Here it is for a household's four lifelines: income, medical care, the home and the phone. Paraphrased from common professional practice; content only, the screen is not built yet. India-specific pointers carry a where tag and say where to confirm. Not legal, medical or financial advice.
status: draft: written 2026-11-15; confirm each India pointer against its official source before the screen ships

rungs.P: Primary: what you use every day.
rungs.A: Alternate: works nearly as well, ready now.
rungs.C: Contingency: slower or costlier, but it works.
rungs.E: Emergency: the last resort that keeps you safe for a few days.

loop.cue: One plan a week for four weeks, then a 20-minute family drill every six months (calendar item proposed: council-pace-drill).
loop.smallestStep: Name the Alternate for one lifeline: one line, two minutes.
loop.reward: The plan's four letters light up one by one; a full plan shows as ready.
loop.environment: The finished plans print as one wallet card and one page for the emergency file.
loop.review: After any job change, move, new phone or new diagnosis, and at the six-month drill.
loop.constraint: The Alternate is the rung people skip: a plan with P and E only is not a plan.

plans.lens: Military planner: decide the fallback before you need it, because under stress people freeze.
plans.question: If the main income stopped this month, what happens in week 1, month 1 and month 6?
plans.trigger: A missed salary or payment, a notice period starting, or sales down by a third for two months.

P.what: The main job or business income.
P.ready: Know your essential monthly cost (the app works it out).

A.what: A second income that already exists: the partner's pay, rent, a retainer or freelance client.
A.ready: Keep one skill, licence or client warm: one piece of paid or visible work every quarter.

C.what: The emergency fund, then cutting to essentials only.
C.ready: Six months of essential costs in a separate account; a written list of what gets cut first.

E.what: Cover and credit you arranged in advance, then family help.
E.ready: Term and health cover paid up; an unused credit line; one honest talk with the person you would ask.

plans.card: Essentials per month: ... | Fund lasts: ... months | First three cuts: ... | Who I call about work: ...

drill.how: Live one month on the essentials budget, or simply check the fund still covers six months at today's costs.

plans.confirm: Your own figures; the single points of failure in council.json (one-earner)

plans.lens: Emergency doctor: the first hour decides most outcomes, and families lose it deciding where to go and how to pay.
plans.question: At 2 a.m., who do we call, where do we go, and how is it paid?
plans.trigger: Chest pain, breathlessness, a fall, a fit, heavy bleeding, sudden weakness on one side, a child who cannot be woken.

P.what: The family doctor and the nearest good hospital on your insurer's cashless list.
P.ready: Save both numbers; keep the health card and policy number in the phone's emergency info.

A.what: A second hospital with an emergency room, in another direction.
A.ready: Check it is on the cashless list too; know the route.

C.what: Any emergency room, paid by card or a medical cash reserve, claimed back later.
C.ready: A card with a free limit and a small cash reserve; know the insurer's reimbursement steps.

E.what: The national emergency number and the nearest neighbour who can drive.
E.ready: Emergency number saved by every family member; two neighbours' numbers; a medical card (blood group, allergies, medicines) in each wallet.

pointers.text: 112 is the single emergency number (police, fire, ambulance); for an ambulance, 108 in many states and 102 in some: confirm yours.

plans.card: Doctor: ... | Hospital 1: ... | Hospital 2: ... | Policy no. and helpline: ... | Blood group, allergies, medicines: ... | Who decides if I cannot: ...

drill.how: Each family member finds the card and says where they would go. Drive the route to hospital 2 once.

plans.confirm: Your insurer's cashless hospital list and your doctor

plans.lens: Diplomat: always know where you would sleep tonight if you could not go home.
plans.question: If the home were unusable tonight (fire, flood, a long power or water cut, a dispute), where do we sleep and what do we take?
plans.trigger: An official warning, water entering, smoke, no power or water for more than a day, or any threat to safety at home.

P.what: The home, with its basics working.
P.ready: Know where the main switch, gas valve and water valve are; a torch and a charged power bank in one known place.

A.what: A relative's or friend's home nearby, agreed in advance.
A.ready: Ask them now, and offer the same in return.

C.what: A hotel or serviced flat, paid from the emergency fund.
C.ready: One or two places saved; home insurance that covers alternative accommodation where offered.

E.what: The public shelter or the family's home town.
E.ready: A go-bag: copies of identity and property papers, medicines for a week, cash, chargers, a spare key.

plans.card: Meet at: ... | Stay with: ... | Go-bag is in: ... | Papers copy is in: ... | Society or landlord: ...

drill.how: Before the rainy season: open the go-bag, replace medicines, check the document copies open on a second device.

plans.lens: Signals officer: assume the main channel will fail at the worst moment.
plans.question: If the phone were lost, stolen or dead, how do we reach each other and our money?
plans.trigger: The phone is missing for an hour, the SIM stops working without reason, or an unknown login or payment appears.

P.what: Your phone, locked, with a passkey or app-based second step.
P.ready: Screen lock on; find-my-device on; backups on.

A.what: A second device or number already registered with the bank and e-mail.
A.ready: Add it now; print the backup codes for e-mail and the password manager and keep them with the papers.

C.what: The partner's phone, to block the SIM and payment apps and to sign in with backup codes.
C.ready: The telco's and bank's helplines on the wallet card; each partner knows the other's blocking steps.

E.what: Family numbers known by heart, and a meeting place.
E.ready: Two numbers memorised by everyone, children included; one agreed place to meet.

pointers.text: A lost or stolen handset can be blocked through the government's Sanchar Saathi service; cyber fraud is reported on the national helpline 1930 and the national cybercrime portal.
pointers.confirm: The Department of Telecommunications and the national cybercrime portal

plans.card: Telco helpline: ... | Bank helpline: ... | Second device: ... | Backup codes are in: ... | Two numbers by heart: ... | Meet at: ...

drill.how: Put the phone in a drawer for an evening: sign in to e-mail and the bank from the second device with the backup path.

plans.confirm: Your bank, telco and e-mail provider; council.json (one-phone)
